title: Private money to organizations with official findings, charges or proven cases
question: Which private funders paid organizations that carry an official finding, a charge or a proven case, in which years, and did the money stop afterwards?
finding: 74 of the 85 City-paid nonprofits that carry an official finding, a charge or a proven case in this project received $343.1 million from the funders on file in 2020 to 2025; the 1 tied to a charged or proven case received $0, the most going to Providence Foundation of San Francisco ($0, 0 funders). Whether funding stopped can be tested for only 3 organizations with grants on file and a dated enforcement step early enough for a later year of returns: for 1 no later grant was found (Bayview Hunters Pt Fndtn For Comm Improv, after “Controller's audit of the UCHS grants, for which the foundation had been …” on 2022-11-17: no grant found in tax periods ending after 2022; $219,886 before), and 2 received grants in later years (Community Housing Partnership, after “Controller publishes the audit.” on 2024-04-02: 3 funders paid $653,300 in tax periods ending after 2024; $3.9 million up to then; Urban Ed Academy, after “District Attorney charges Jones and Henriquez.” on 2023-08-29: 8 funders paid $810,841 in tax periods ending after 2023; $2.7 million up to then).
how: Organizations are the City-paid nonprofits whose strongest sign in this project's flag file is an official finding (for example findings left open in the City's fiscal monitoring, a weakness reported by auditors, a suspended registration), a charged case or a proven case. Their grants from the funders on file are added by the calendar year in which the funder's tax period ends. A date is taken only from a case file with an official finding, charge or proven conduct that is about that organization: the file's first enforcement step where the case charts that organization alone or names it in its summary, otherwise the first step whose text names it. The step is printed beside the date. 'Paid in later years' counts grants in funder tax periods ending in calendar years after that step. Rows: proven, then charged, then official findings, largest private total first.
limits: A grant to an organization is not a grant to the person charged, and in several cases the organization is a witness or a fiscal sponsor, not the accused. Most official findings here are administrative and no reason in themselves for a funder to withdraw. The first enforcement step is often an audit, not a charge. Tax periods ending in 2025 are incomplete in the IRS release, so for most 2024 to 2026 steps no later year is on file. Nothing here shows a funder knew of a finding when it paid. Matching is by employer number or name.
